181:   * **If a serif is justified** (rare, per the above), rotate from this pool, do NOT reuse the same serif across consecutive projects: PP Editorial New, GT Sectra Display, Cardinal Grotesque, Reckless Neue, Tiempos Headline, Recoleta, Cormorant Garamond, Playfair Display, EB Garamond, IvyPresto, Migra, Editorial Old, Saol Display, Söhne Breit Kursiv, Domaine Display, Canela, Schnyder, Tobias, NB Architekt, ITC Galliard.

185: ### 4.2 Color Calibration

189: * **One palette per project.** Do not fluctuate between warm and cool grays within the same project.
190: * **COLOR CONSISTENCY LOCK (mandatory):** Once an accent color is chosen for a page, it is used on the WHOLE page. A warm-grey site does not suddenly get a blue CTA in section 7. A rose-accented site does not get a teal status badge in the footer. Pick one accent, lock it, audit every component before shipping.
191: 
192: * **PREMIUM-CONSUMER PALETTE BAN (mandatory, second-most-recurring AI-tell):**
193:   * For premium-consumer briefs (cookware, wellness, artisan, luxury, heritage craft, DTC home goods, etc.) the LLM default is **warm beige/cream + brass/clay/oxblood/ochre + espresso/ink dark text**. Concretely banned hex families as default backgrounds and accents:
194:     - Backgrounds: `#f5f1ea`, `#f7f5f1`, `#fbf8f1`, `#efeae0`, `#ece6db`, `#faf7f1`, `#e8dfcb` (all "warm paper / cream / chalk / bone")
195:     - Accents: `#b08947`, `#b6553a`, `#9a2436`, `#9c6e2a`, `#bc7c3a`, `#7d5621` (all "brass / clay / oxblood / ochre")
196:     - Text: `#1a1714`, `#1a1814`, `#1b1814` (all "espresso / warm near-black")
197:   * This palette is BANNED as the default reach for premium-consumer briefs. Every premium-consumer site you have ever shipped uses this exact palette. The brand becomes invisible.
198:   * **Default alternatives (rotate, do not reuse):**
199:     - **Cold Luxury:** silver-grey + chrome + smoke (think Tesla, Apple Watch Hermes-without-the-leather)
200:     - **Forest:** deep green + bone + amber accent (think Filson, Patagonia premium)
201:     - **Black and Tan:** true off-black + warm tan, sharp contrast, no beige
202:     - **Cobalt + Cream:** saturated blue against a single neutral, no brass
203:     - **Terracotta + Slate:** warm rust against cool grey, no brass
204:     - **Olive + Brick + Paper:** muted olive plus brick-red accent
205:     - **Pure monochrome + single saturated pop:** off-white + off-black + one bright accent (electric blue, emerald, hot pink, etc.)
206:   * **Palette-rotation rule:** if the previous premium-consumer project you generated used the beige+brass family, this one MUST use a different family. Do not ship the same warm-craft palette twice in a row.
207:   * **Override:** the beige+brass+espresso palette is acceptable ONLY when the brand brief explicitly names those colors, or when the brand identity is genuinely vintage / artisan / warm-craft AND you can articulate why this specific palette fits this specific brand. Default-reaching for it because "this is a cookware brief" is banned.

209: ### 4.3 Layout Diversification
210: * **ANTI-CENTER BIAS:** Centered Hero / H1 sections are avoided when `DESIGN_VARIANCE > 4`. Force "Split Screen" (50/50), "Left-aligned content / right-aligned asset", "Asymmetric white-space", or scroll-pinned structures.

213: ### 4.4 Materiality, Shadows, Cards

215: * When a shadow is used, tint it to the background hue. No pure-black drop shadows on light backgrounds.

222: * **Empty States:** Beautifully composed; indicate how to populate.
223: * **Error States:** Clear, inline (forms), or contextual (toasts only for transient).
224: * **Tactile Feedback:** On `:active`, use `-translate-y-[1px]` or `scale-[0.98]` to simulate a physical push.
225: * **BUTTON CONTRAST CHECK (mandatory, a11y):** Before shipping any button, verify the button text is readable against the button background. White button + white text, `bg-white` CTA with `text-white` label, transparent button against the page background with no border → all banned. Audit every CTA: contrast ratio WCAG AA min (4.5:1 for body, 3:1 for large text 18px+). Same rule applies to ghost buttons over photographic backgrounds (use a backdrop, scrim, or stroke).
226: * **CTA BUTTON WRAP BAN (mandatory):** Button text MUST fit on one line at desktop. If a label like "VIEW SELECTED WORK" wraps to 2 or 3 lines, the button is broken. Fix by EITHER shortening the label (3 words max for primary CTAs, ideally 1-2) OR widening the button (do not artificially constrain `max-width` on CTAs). Wrapped CTAs at desktop are a Pre-Flight Fail.
227: * **NO DUPLICATE CTA INTENT (mandatory):** Two CTAs with the same intent on one page is a Pre-Flight Fail. Examples of same intent: "Get in touch" + "Contact us" + "Let's talk" + "Start a project" + "Start something" + "Reach out" = all "contact" intent → pick ONE label and use it everywhere on the page (nav, hero, footer). Same for "Try free" + "Get started" + "Sign up free" (all "signup" intent) and "View work" + "See selected work" + "Browse projects" (all "portfolio" intent). One label per intent.
228: * **FORM CONTRAST CHECK (mandatory, a11y):** Form inputs, placeholder text, focus rings, helper text, and error text all pass WCAG AA contrast against the section background. Light placeholders on a near-white form, white form on white page section, form labels grayer than 4.5:1 contrast → all banned. Audit every form before shipping.
229: 
230: ### 4.6 Data & Form Patterns
231: * Label ABOVE input. Helper text optional but present in markup. Error text BELOW input. Standard `gap-2` for input blocks.
232: * No placeholder-as-label. Ever.
233: 
234: ### 4.7 Layout Discipline (Hard Rules. Failing any of these is shipping broken work)
235: 
236: * **Hero MUST fit in the initial viewport.** Headline max 2 lines on desktop, subtext max **20 words** AND max 3-4 lines, CTAs visible without scroll. If the copy is too long: reduce font scale OR cut copy. If you cannot describe the value-prop in 20 words of subtext, the value-prop is unclear, not the rule too tight. Never let the hero overflow and force scroll to find the CTA.
237: * **Hero font-scale discipline.** Plan font size and image size *together*. If the hero asset is large and the headline is more than 6 words, do not start at `text-7xl/text-8xl`. Default sensible range: `text-4xl md:text-5xl lg:text-6xl` for most heroes; `text-6xl md:text-7xl` only when the headline is 3-5 words. A 4-line hero headline is always a font-size error, never a copy-length error.
238: * **HERO TOP PADDING CAP (mandatory):** Hero top padding max `pt-24` (≈6rem) at desktop. More than that means the hero content floats halfway down the viewport and reads as a layout bug, not as intentional space. If your hero needs more breathing room, increase font scale or asset size, not top padding.
239: * **HERO STACK DISCIPLINE (max 4 text elements).** The hero is a single moment, not a feature list. Allowed text elements, max 4 in total:
240:   1. Eyebrow (small uppercase label) OR brand strip OR neither - pick zero or one
241:   2. Headline (max 2 lines, see above)
242:   3. Subtext (max 20 words, max 4 lines)
243:   4. CTAs (1 primary + max 1 secondary)
244:   - **BANNED in the hero:** tiny tagline below CTAs ("Works with GitHub, GitLab, and self-hosted Git"), trust micro-strip ("Used by engineering teams at..."), pricing teaser ("Free for solo, $10/user for teams"), feature bullet list, social-proof avatar row. All of those move to dedicated sections directly below the hero.
245:   - If you have an eyebrow AND a tagline below CTAs in the same hero, drop the tagline. If you have a brand strip AND a tagline, drop the tagline. One small text element per hero, max.
246: * **"Used by" / "Trusted by" logo wall belongs UNDER the hero, never inside it.** The hero is for the value prop and primary CTA. The logo wall is a separate section directly below. Do not stuff trust logos into the same flex row as the hero copy.
247: * **Navigation MUST render on a single line on desktop.** If items don't fit at `lg` (1024px), condense labels, drop secondary items, or move to a hamburger. A two-line nav at desktop is broken design.
248: * **Navigation height cap: 80px max desktop, default 64-72px.** No huge "agency" nav bars that eat 15% of the viewport.
249: * **Bento grids MUST have rhythm, not one-sided repetition.** Do not stack 6 left-image / right-text rows. Vary the composition: alternate full-width feature rows, asymmetric tile sizes, vertical breaks.
250: * **BENTO CELL COUNT RULE (mandatory):** A bento grid has EXACTLY as many cells as you have content for. 3 items → 3 cells (1+2 split, or 2+1, or asymmetric trio). 5 items → 5 cells (2+3, 3+2, hero+4, etc.). If your grid has an empty cell in the middle or at the end, you planned wrong. Re-shape the grid; do not paste a blank tile.
251: * **Section-Layout-Repetition Ban.** Once you use a layout family for a section (e.g., 3-column-image-cards, full-width-quote, split-text-image), that family can appear at most ONCE on the page. "Selected commissions" must not look like "What we do." A landing page with 8 sections must use at least 4 different layout families.
252: * **ZIGZAG ALTERNATION CAP (mandatory).** Alternating "left-image + right-text" then "left-text + right-image" zigzag layout = banal. Max 2 sections in a row with this image+text-split pattern. The 3rd consecutive image+text split is a Pre-Flight Fail. Break the pattern with a full-width section, a vertical-stack section, a bento grid, a marquee, or a different layout family.
253: * **EYEBROW RESTRAINT (mandatory, the #1 violated rule in production tests).** An "eyebrow" is the small uppercase wide-tracking label sitting above a section headline (e.g. `FOUR COLORWAYS`, `SELECTED WORK`, `THE HARDWARE`, `Git-native task management`). Typical CSS signature: `text-[11px] uppercase tracking-[0.18em]`, `font-mono text-[10.5px] uppercase tracking-[0.22em]`. Every AI-built site puts an eyebrow above EVERY section header, producing the same templated rhythm. Hard rule:
254:   - **Maximum 1 eyebrow per 3 sections.** Hero counts as 1. So a page with 9 sections may use at most 3 eyebrows total.
255:   - If section A has an eyebrow, the next 2 sections cannot have one.
256:   - **Pre-Flight Check is mechanical:** count instances of `uppercase tracking` (or similar small-caps mono labels above headlines) across all section components. If count > ceil(sectionCount / 3), the output fails.
257:   - **What to do instead of an eyebrow:** drop it entirely. The headline alone is enough. If you need to categorize a section, the section's location on the page already categorizes it; no label needed.
258: * **SPLIT-HEADER BAN (mandatory).** The pattern "left big headline + right small explainer paragraph" as a section header (left col-span-7/8, right col-span-4/5 with a small body paragraph floating in the right column) is **banned as default**. Sections should have ONE focused message. If you genuinely need both a headline and an explainer paragraph, stack them vertically (headline on top, body below, max-width 65ch). Reach for the split-header pattern only when there is a real compositional reason (e.g., the right column carries a visual or interactive element, not just filler text).
259: * **Bento Background Diversity (mandatory).** Bento and feature-grid sections cannot be 6 white-on-white cards with text inside. At least 2-3 cells in any multi-cell grid need real visual variation: a real image, a brand-appropriate gradient (not AI-purple), a pattern, a tinted background. A cream-on-cream bento with only typography inside reads as boring AI default, even when the rest of the page is good.
260: * **Mobile collapse must be explicit per section.** For every multi-column layout, declare the `< 768px` fallback in the same component. No "it'll work, Tailwind handles it" assumptions.
261: 
262: ### 4.8 Image & Visual Asset Strategy
263: 
264: Landing pages and portfolios are **visual products**. Text-only pages with fake-screenshot divs are slop.
265: 
266: **Priority order for visual assets:**
267: 1. **Image-generation tool first.** If ANY image-gen tool is available in the environment (`generate_image`, MCP image tool, IDE-integrated gen, OpenAI image tools, etc.) you MUST use it to create section-specific assets: hero photography, product shots, texture backgrounds, mood images. Generate at the right aspect ratio for the section. Do not skip this step because hand-rolled CSS feels faster.
268: 2. **Real web images second.** When no gen tool is available, use real photography sources. Acceptable defaults:
269:    * `https://picsum.photos/seed/{descriptive-seed}/{w}/{h}` for placeholder photography (seed should describe the section, e.g. `marrow-cookware-kitchen`)
270:    * Actual stock or brand URLs when the brief provides them
271:    * Open-license sources (Unsplash via direct URL, Pexels) if explicitly allowed
272: 3. **Last resort: tell the user.** If neither is possible, do NOT fill the page with hand-rolled SVG illustrations or div-based "fake screenshots." Instead, leave clearly-labeled placeholder slots (`<!-- TODO: hero product photo, 1600x1200 -->`) and at the end of the response say: *"This page needs real images at: \[list of placements\]. Please generate or provide them."*
273: 
274: **Even minimalist sites need real images.** A pure-text page is not minimalism. It is incomplete work. Even an editorial Linear-style site needs at least 2-3 real images (hero, one product/lifestyle shot, one supporting image). Generate B&W minimalist photography if the brief is restrained; do not skip images entirely because the dial is low.
275: 
276: **Real company logos for social proof.** When the brief calls for a "Trusted by / Used by / Customers" logo wall, do NOT default to plain text wordmarks (`<span>Acme Co</span>` styled in a row). Use real SVG logos:
277: * **Source: Simple Icons** (`https://cdn.simpleicons.org/{slug}/ffffff` for any color, or `simple-icons` npm package). Covers most known brands.
278: * **Alternative: devicon** for tech-stack logos (`@svgr/cli` or CDN).
279: * **Make-up the brand name? Then make-up an SVG mark too.** Generate a simple monogram (one letter in a circle, two-letter ligature, abstract glyph) rendered as an inline `<svg>` matching the page style. Plain text wordmarks for invented brand names look generic.
280: * **Always** ensure logos render in both light and dark mode (white-on-dark, black-on-light, or single-color theme variable).
281: * **LOGO-ONLY rule (mandatory):** logo wall = logos and nothing else. Do NOT print industry / category labels below each logo (no `Vercel` + `hosting` underneath, no `Stripe` + `payments`, no `Cloudflare` + `infra`). The logo is the credibility, the label adds nothing the user does not already know. Optional: brand name as alt-text for screen readers, optional link to the brand's site. That is it.
282: 
283: **Hand-rolled illustrations:**
284: * SVG icons from libraries: fine (see Section 3.C).
285: * Hand-rolled decorative SVGs (custom illustrations, logos, marks): **strongly discouraged**, never as default. Acceptable only when:
286:   - The brief explicitly calls for it ("draw me an SVG logo")
287:   - It's a single, simple geometric mark (a square, a circle, a wordmark in display type)
288:   - You're confident in the output quality
289: 
290: **Div-based fake screenshots are banned.** A "hand-built product preview" rendered with `<div>` rectangles, fake task lists, fake dashboards, fake terminal windows is a Tell. If you need to show a product:
291: * Use a real screenshot URL if one exists
292: * Generate one via image tool
293: * Use a real component preview (an actual mini-version of the UI inside the page)
294: * Or skip the preview entirely and use editorial photography
295: 
296: **Hero needs a real visual.** Text + gradient blob is not a hero - it's a placeholder.
297: 
298: ### 4.9 Content Density
299: 
300: Landing pages live on the **first impression**, not the full read. Cut ruthlessly.
301: 
302: * **Default content shape per section:** short headline (≤ 8 words) + short sub-paragraph (≤ 25 words) + one visual asset OR one CTA. Anything more must be justified by the section's job.
303: * **No data-dump sections.** A 20-row publication table, a 30-row award list, a giant pricing matrix on a marketing page = wrong layout. Use:
304:   - Top 3-5 highlights + "View full list" link
305:   - Marquee / carousel for breadth
306:   - Different page entirely if the data is the product
307: * **Long lists need a different UI component, not a longer list.** Default `<ul>` with bullets / `divide-y` rows is the lazy choice. If you have > 5 items, reach for one of these instead:
308:   - 2-column split with grouped items
309:   - Card grid with image + label per item
310:   - Tabs / accordion if items are categorisable
311:   - Horizontal scroll-snap pills
312:   - Carousel for breadth-heavy lists (testimonials, logos, capabilities)
313:   - Marquee for "lots-of-things-that-don't-need-individual-attention"
314:   A spec sheet with 10 rows + a hairline under every row is the WORST default. Either group rows into 2-3 chunks with sparse dividers, or move to a card-per-spec layout.
315: * **Spec sheets specifically (the Marrow-cookware pattern).** A long product specification table with `border-b` on every row is the AI default for cookware / hardware / apparel / artisan-goods briefs. Banned. Concrete alternatives:
316:   - **2-col card grid:** each spec gets its own card with the spec name, the value (large display number), and a one-line "why it matters" body. Cards arranged 2-col on desktop, 1-col mobile.
317:   - **Scroll-snap horizontal pills:** each spec is a pill, user can flick through.
318:   - **Grouped chunks:** group 10 specs into 3 logical clusters (e.g. "Materials", "Cooking", "Warranty"), each cluster gets ONE soft divider and a cluster heading.
319:   - **Featured-vs-rest:** 3-4 hero specs visualised as large display tiles, the rest collapsed under a "View full specifications" disclosure.
320: 
321: * **COPY SELF-AUDIT (mandatory before ship):** Before declaring any task done, re-read every visible string on the page (headlines, subheads, eyebrows, button labels, body copy, captions, alt text, footer text, error messages). Flag any string that is:
322:   - **Grammatically broken** ("free on its past", "two plans but one is honest", "to put it on the table" out of context)
323:   - **Has unclear referents** ("we plan to stay that way" without prior context)
324:   - **Sounds like AI hallucination** (cute-but-wrong wordplay, forced metaphors that don't track, "elegant nothing" phrases)
325:   - **Reads like an LLM trying to sound thoughtful** (passive-aggressive humility, fake-craftsman labels, mock-poetic micro-meta)
326:   Rewrite every flagged string. If unsure whether a string makes sense, replace it with a plain functional sentence. AI-generated cute copy is worse than boring copy.
327: * **Fake-precise numbers are flagged.** Numbers like `92%`, `4.1×`, `48k`, `5.8 mm`, `13.4 lb` either:
328:   - Come from real data (brief, brand guidelines, public metrics) - fine
329:   - Are explicitly labeled as mock (`<!-- mock -->`, "example", "sample data") - fine
330:   - Are AI-invented spec aesthetics - banned. Don't fake engineering precision the brand doesn't claim.
331: * **One copy register per page.** Don't mix technical mono ("47 tasks · 0.6 ctx-switches/day"), editorial prose, and marketing punch in the same composition unless the brand voice explicitly calls for it.
332: 
333: ### 4.10 Quotes & Testimonials
334: 
335: * **Max 3 lines** of quote body. Never 6. If the original quote is longer → cut it. A landing-page quote is a snippet, not the full review.
336: * For very small font sizes (e.g. footer-style testimonials), the line cap can stretch slightly. Spirit: "fits in a glance."
337: * **No em-dashes inside the quote text** as design flourish (long pauses, kinetic em-dashes, em-dash-bullets). See Section 9.G - em-dash is completely banned.
338: * Attribution: name + role + (optionally) company. Never name only ("- Sarah").
339: * Quote marks: use real typographic quotes ( " " ) or none at all. Not straight ASCII ( " ).
340: 
341: ### 4.11 Page Theme Lock (Light / Dark Mode Consistency)
342: 
343: The page has ONE theme. Sections do not invert.
344: 
345: * If the page is dark mode, ALL sections are dark mode. No light-mode-warm-paper section sandwiched between dark sections (or vice versa). The user must not feel they walked into a different website mid-scroll.
346: * The exception: if the brief explicitly calls for a "Color Block Story" or "Theme Switch on Scroll" device AND that is a deliberate composition (one full theme switch with a strong transition, not random alternation), it is allowed once per page.
347: * Default behaviour: pick light, dark, or auto (`prefers-color-scheme`) at the page level and lock it. Section-level background tints within the same theme family are fine (`bg-zinc-950` next to `bg-zinc-900`); flipping to `bg-amber-50` in the middle of a `bg-zinc-950` page is broken.
348: * When using a design system with built-in theming (Radix Themes, shadcn/ui with `<Theme>`), set the theme ONCE in `layout.tsx` or the page root. Do not let individual sections override.

352: ## 5. CONTEXT-AWARE PROACTIVITY
353: 
354: These are tools, not defaults. Use them when the design read calls for them. **None of these fire automatically.**
355: 
356: * **Liquid Glass / Glassmorphism:** Appropriate for premium consumer, Apple-adjacent, luxury brand, or media-overlay vibes. Inappropriate for dashboards, public-sector, or "boring B2B." When used, go beyond `backdrop-blur`: add a 1px inner border (`border-white/10`) and a subtle inner shadow (`shadow-[inset_0_1px_0_rgba(255,255,255,0.1)]`) for physical edge refraction. Provide a solid-fill fallback under `prefers-reduced-transparency`.
357: * **Magnetic Micro-physics:** Use when `MOTION_INTENSITY > 5` AND the brief reads premium / playful / agency. Implement EXCLUSIVELY with Motion's `useMotionValue` / `useTransform` outside the React render cycle. Never `useState`. See Section 3.B.
358: * **Perpetual Micro-Interactions** (Pulse, Typewriter, Float, Shimmer, Carousel): Use when `MOTION_INTENSITY > 5` AND the section actively benefits from motion (status indicators, live feeds, AI-feel). **Not every card needs an infinite loop.** If a section is informational, leave it still. Apply Spring Physics (`type: "spring", stiffness: 100, damping: 20`) - no linear easing.
359: * **"Motion claimed, motion shown."** If `MOTION_INTENSITY > 4`, the page must actually move: entry transitions on hero, scroll-reveal on key sections, hover physics on CTAs, at minimum. A static page that claims `MOTION_INTENSITY: 7` is broken. Conversely, if you cannot ship working motion in the available scope, drop the dial to 3 and ship a clean static page. Never half-build motion that breaks (cut-off ScrollTriggers, jumpy enters, missing cleanups).
360: * **MOTION MUST BE MOTIVATED (mandatory).** Before adding any animation, ask: "what does this animation communicate?" Valid answers: hierarchy (drawing attention to the right thing), storytelling (revealing content in sequence that matches a narrative), feedback (acknowledging a user action), state transition (showing something changed). Invalid answer: "it looked cool". GSAP everywhere because GSAP is available is amateur. Each ScrollTrigger, each marquee, each pinned section needs a reason. If you cannot articulate the reason in one sentence, drop the animation.
361: * **MARQUEE MAX-ONE-PER-PAGE (mandatory).** Horizontal scrolling text marquees ("logos endlessly scrolling", "manifesto scrolling sideways", "kinetic word strip") are appropriate at most ONCE per page. Two or more marquees on the same page reads as lazy filler. Pick the one section where the marquee actually serves the content; the others get a different layout.
362: * **GSAP Sticky-Stack Pattern (when scroll-stack is used).** A "card stack on scroll" must be a REAL sticky-stack, not a sequential reveal list. See Section 5.A below for the canonical code skeleton. Common failure: trigger fires halfway through scroll instead of pinning at viewport top. Fix: `start: "top top"` not `start: "top center"` or `"top 80%"`.
363: * **GSAP Horizontal-Pan Pattern (when horizontal scroll-hijack is used).** See Section 5.B below for the canonical skeleton. Common failure: animation starts before the section is pinned, so the user sees half a slide. Same fix: `start: "top top"`, pin the wrapper, scrub the inner track.
364: 
365: ### 5.A Sticky-Stack - Canonical Skeleton
366: 
367: ```tsx
368: "use client";
369: import { useRef, useEffect } from "react";
370: import { gsap } from "gsap";
371: import { ScrollTrigger } from "gsap/ScrollTrigger";
372: import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react";
373: 
374: gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger);
375: 
376: export function StickyStack({ cards }: { cards: React.ReactNode[] }) {
377:   const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
378:   const reduce = useReducedMotion();
379: 
380:   useEffect(() => {
381:     if (reduce || !ref.current) return;
382:     const ctx = gsap.context(() => {
383:       const cardEls = gsap.utils.toArray<HTMLElement>(".stack-card");
384:       cardEls.forEach((card, i) => {
385:         if (i === cardEls.length - 1) return;
386:         ScrollTrigger.create({
387:           trigger: card,
388:           start: "top top",                              // pin at viewport top
389:           endTrigger: cardEls[cardEls.length - 1],
390:           end: "top top",
391:           pin: true,
392:           pinSpacing: false,
393:         });
394:         gsap.to(card, {
395:           scale: 0.92,
396:           opacity: 0.55,
397:           ease: "none",
398:           scrollTrigger: {
399:             trigger: cardEls[i + 1],
400:             start: "top bottom",
401:             end: "top top",
402:             scrub: true,
403:           },
404:         });
405:       });
406:     }, ref);
407:     return () => ctx.revert();
408:   }, [reduce]);
409: 
410:   return (
411:     <div ref={ref} className="relative">
412:       {cards.map((card, i) => (
413:         <div
414:           key={i}
415:           className="stack-card sticky top-0 min-h-[100dvh] flex items-center justify-center"
416:         >
417:           {card}
418:         </div>
419:       ))}
420:     </div>
421:   );
422: }
423: ```
424: 
425: Critical points: `start: "top top"`, `pin: true`, every card except the last is pinned, the scale/opacity transform is driven by the NEXT card's scroll trigger (so previous card shrinks as next one arrives).

PERFORMANCE & ACCESSIBILITY GUARDRAILS 520: 521: ### 6.A Hardware Acceleration 522: * Animate ONLY `transform` and `opacity`. Never animate `top`, `left`, `width`, `height`. 523: * Use `will-change: transform` sparingly - only on elements that will actually animate. 524: 525: ### 6.B Reduced Motion (mandatory) 526: * **Any motion above `MOTION_INTENSITY > 3` MUST honor `prefers-reduced-motion`.** This is non-negotiable. 527: * In Motion: wrap with `useReducedMotion()` and degrade to static. 528: * In CSS: gate animations behind `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` or provide an override block under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` that disables. 529: * Infinite loops, parallax, scroll-hijack, and magnetic physics MUST collapse to static / instant under reduced motion. 530: 531: ### 6.C Dark Mode (mandatory for any consumer-facing page) 532: * Design for **both modes from the start**. Never ship light-only or dark-only without explicit user instruction. 533: * Use Tailwind `dark:` variant OR CSS variables for tokens. Pick one strategy per project. 534: * **Do not prescribe specific dark-mode colors here.** The brief decides. Maintain visual hierarchy, brand identity, and WCAG AA contrast (AAA for body) across both modes. 535: * Respect `prefers-color-scheme: dark`. # arXiv Search and Retrieval

## Core Rules

- **Terms of Use**: You MUST respect arXiv's Terms of Use (`https://info.arxiv.org/help/api/index.html`).
  - Maximum 1 request every 3 seconds.
  - The provided utility scripts below `/workspace/skills/literature-search-arxiv/scripts/` handle rate limiting automatically. Always use these scripts rather than writing ad-hoc curl requests.
- If this skill is used, mention arXiv in the output AND list the URLs of all papers that were used in producing the output.

## Utility Scripts

Once loaded via `skill_load(name="literature-search-arxiv")`, the scripts are located in `/workspace/skills/literature-search-arxiv/scripts/` and run with standard `python3` (zero external package dependencies required).

**1. Search and Extract Metadata**

Search arXiv and return a clean JSON array of matching papers:

```bash
python3 /workspace/skills/literature-search-arxiv/scripts/search_arxiv.py \
  --query "au:einstein AND ti:relativity" \
  --max_results 5 > /tmp/arxiv_search_results.json
```

> **Important**: Limit `--max_results` (e.g., 5–10) or paginate carefully using `--start`. Redirect output to a file or inspect cleanly.

*Returned Metadata:* JSON results include `id`, `title`, `summary`, `published`, `authors`, `pdf_url`, `primary_category`, `doi`, `journal_ref`, and `comment`.

*Options:*
- `--query`: Search string. See [references/query_syntax.md](references/query_syntax.md) for advanced syntax (`ti:`, `au:`, `abs:`, `cat:`, `AND`, `OR`, `ANDNOT`).
- `--id_list`: Comma-separated list of arXiv IDs to fetch directly (e.g., `1706.03762v5`).
- `--start`: Pagination offset (default 0).
- `--max_results`: Number of results to return (default 10).
- `--sort_by`: `relevance`, `lastUpdatedDate`, or `submittedDate`.
- `--sort_order`: `ascending` or `descending`.

**2. Download Paper (PDF or HTML)**

Download the full text of a paper to your local workspace:

```bash
python3 /workspace/skills/literature-search-arxiv/scripts/download_paper.py \
  --id 1706.03762 --format html --output /workspace/attention.html
```

*Options:*
- `--id`: The arXiv ID (e.g., `1706.03762` or `1706.03762v5`).
- `--format`: `pdf` or `html` (HTML is available for many newer papers and is easy to read directly).
- `--output`: Filepath to save the downloaded document.

**3. Download Paper Source (tar.gz)**

Download the LaTeX source files of a paper:

```bash
python3 /workspace/skills/literature-search-arxiv/scripts/download_paper_source.py \
  --id 2010.11645 --output /workspace/source.tar.gz
```

> **Safe Extraction**: Always extract into a dedicated directory: `mkdir -p /workspace/paper_source && tar -xzf /workspace/source.tar.gz -C /workspace/paper_source`

## Reference

- **Advanced Query Syntax**: See `/workspace/skills/literature-search-arxiv/references/query_syntax.md` for prefixes (`au`, `ti`, `abs`, `cat`), booleans, and date filtering.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Downloads a paper from arXiv given its ID (PDF or HTML)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

_USER_AGENT = "VigilAgent-ArxivSearch/1.0 (https://info.arxiv.org/help/api/index.html)"


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Download paper from arXiv (PDF or HTML)")
    parser.add_argument("--id", type=str, required=True, help="arXiv ID (e.g., 2305.10601)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--format",
        type=str,
        choices=["pdf", "html"],
        required=True,
        help="Download format",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=str, required=True, help="Output file path")
    return parser.parse_args()


def download_paper(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    paper_id = args.id.strip()
    if args.format == "pdf":
        url = f"https://arxiv.org/pdf/{paper_id}.pdf"
    elif args.format == "html":
        url = f"https://arxiv.org/html/{paper_id}"
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported format: {args.format}")

    print(f"Attempting to download {args.format.upper()} from {url}...")
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": _USER_AGENT})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60.0) as resp:
            content = resp.read()
        out_dir = os.path.dirname(args.output)
        if out_dir:
            os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
        with open(args.output, "wb") as f:
            f.write(content)
        print(f"Success! Saved to {args.output}")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        if e.code == 404 and args.format == "html":
            print(
                f"Error 404: HTML format is not available for this paper (ID: {paper_id}). "
                "Please try --format pdf instead.",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            sys.exit(1)
        raise


if __name__ == "__main__":
    download_paper(parse_args())

        out_dir = os.path.dirname(args.output)
        if out_dir:
            os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
        with open(args.output, "wb") as f:
            f.write(content)
        print(f"Success! Saved to {args.output}")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        if e.code == 404:
            print(
                f"Error 404: Source not found (ID: {paper_id}). Not all papers have source available.",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            sys.exit(1)
        raise


if __name__ == "__main__":
    download_source(parse_args())

---
name: literature-search-openalex
description: >
  Query the OpenAlex scholarly database for research papers, authors,
  institutions, topics, sources, publishers, funders, geo-locations, and
  keywords. Use when searching academic papers, resolving DOIs, downloading
  open-access PDFs, finding an author's publications, aggregating bibliometric
  data (citation counts, h-index, impact factor), exploring the research
  taxonomies, or performing DOI lookups.
version: 1.0.0
---

# OpenAlex Scholarly Research Skill

## Core Rules

1. **List Sources**: If this skill is used, mention OpenAlex in the output AND list the URLs or DOIs of all papers that were used in producing the output.
2. **Resolve before filter**: NEVER filter by name. Always `resolve` a name to an ID first, then use that ID in `--filter`.
3. **Use the CLI**: Once loaded via `skill_load(name="literature-search-openalex")`, invoke `/workspace/skills/literature-search-openalex/scripts/openalex_cli.py` with `python3` (zero external package dependencies required).
4. **No fabrication**: Never invent OpenAlex IDs or DOIs. Use `resolve`/`get` to look them up. Report empty results accurately.
5. **Keep output small**: Always use `--select` and `--per-page 5` to `10` for overview queries.

## CLI Reference

```bash
python3 /workspace/skills/literature-search-openalex/scripts/openalex_cli.py [--api-key KEY] <command> [flags]
```

Entity types (shared across commands): `works`, `authors`, `sources`, `institutions`, `topics`, `domains`, `fields`, `subfields`, `sdgs`, `countries`, `continents`, `languages`, `keywords`, `publishers`, `funders`, `work-types`, `source-types`, `institution-types`, `licenses`

### Commands

- **`resolve <entity> <query>`** — Name → ID candidates. Returns `id`, `display_name`, `hint`. Use `--per-page N` for more candidates.
- **`get <entity> <id>`** — Full metadata for one entity. Accepts short ID (`W2741809807`), full URL, or DOI URL (`https://doi.org/...`). Use `--select` to limit fields.
- **`filter <entity>`** — Search/filter entities:
  - `--search <query>`: Full-text search
  - `--filter <expr>`: Filter expressions (`,` for AND, `|` for OR)
  - `--sort <field:dir>`: Sort results (e.g., `cited_by_count:desc`)
  - `--select <fields>`: Limit fields returned in output
  - `--group-by <field>`: Aggregate results by a field
  - `--per-page <N>`: Results per page (default 25, max 100)
  - `--page <N>`: Page number
- **`download-pdf <work-id> <output-path>`** — Download open-access PDF for a work.
- **`rate-limit`** — Check current rate limit and daily budget status.

## Entity References

Consult `/workspace/skills/literature-search-openalex/references/` for valid filter, sort, and group-by fields per entity (`works.md`, `authors.md`, `sources.md`, `institutions.md`, `topics.md`, `taxonomy.md`).

## Common Workflows

```bash
# Author's works (resolve -> filter)
python3 /workspace/skills/literature-search-openalex/scripts/openalex_cli.py resolve authors "Geoffrey Hinton"
python3 /workspace/skills/literature-search-openalex/scripts/openalex_cli.py filter works \
  --filter "authorships.author.id:A5108093963" \
  --sort "cited_by_count:desc" \
  --select "id,display_name,publication_year,cited_by_count,doi" \
  --per-page 10

# DOI lookup
python3 /workspace/skills/literature-search-openalex/scripts/openalex_cli.py get works "https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2"
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI tool for querying the OpenAlex API.

Uses only the Python standard library so it runs inside any sandbox or host
environment without external package installation, with automatic rate-limit
backoff and PDF fallback downloads.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import os
import random
import re
import sys
import time
from typing import Any, Sequence
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s: %(message)s")

BASE_URL = "https://api.openalex.org"
PDF_BASE_URL = "https://content.openalex.org"
USER_AGENT = "VigilAgent-OpenAlex/1.0 (https://help.openalex.org)"

DEFAULT_PER_PAGE = 25
MAX_PER_PAGE = 100
RESOLVE_PER_PAGE = 5
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECS = 30.0
PDF_TIMEOUT_SECS = 60.0
MAX_RETRIES = 4
TRUNCATE_LINE_LIMIT = 500
PLAN_UPGRADE_ERROR = "Plan upgrade required"

ENTITY_TYPES = [
    "works",
    "authors",
    "sources",
    "institutions",
    "topics",
    "domains",
    "fields",
    "subfields",
    "sdgs",
    "countries",
    "continents",
    "languages",
    "keywords",
    "publishers",
    "funders",
    "awards",
    "work-types",
    "source-types",
    "institution-types",
    "licenses",
]


def _load_dotenv_if_present() -> None:
    env_path = os.path.expanduser("~/.env")
    if not os.path.isfile(env_path):
        return
    try:
        with open(env_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for line in f:
                raw = line.strip()
                if not raw or raw.startswith("#") or "=" not in raw:
                    continue
                k, v = raw.split("=", 1)
                os.environ.setdefault(k.strip(), v.strip().strip("'\""))
    except OSError:
        pass


def _build_url_with_api_key(url: str, api_key: str | None) -> str:
    if not api_key:
        return url
    separator = "&" if "?" in url else "?"
    return f"{url}{separator}{urllib.parse.urlencode({'api_key': api_key})}"


def _http_get(full_url: str, timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECS) -> tuple[bytes, dict[str, str]]:
    req = urllib.request.Request(full_url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
        headers = {k.lower(): v for k, v in resp.headers.items()}
        return resp.read(), headers


def fetch_with_retry(
    url: str,
    params: dict[str, Any],
    api_key: str | None = None,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    exit_on_error: bool = True,
    return_headers: bool = False,
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    query_string = urllib.parse.urlencode(params, doseq=True)
    full_url = f"{url}?{query_string}" if query_string else url
    full_url = _build_url_with_api_key(full_url, api_key)

    for attempt in range(max_retries + 1):
        try:
            body, headers = _http_get(full_url)
            data = json.loads(body.decode("utf-8"))
            if return_headers:
                data["_response_headers"] = headers
            return data
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            err_body = ""
            try:
                err_body = e.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            except Exception:
                pass
            if e.code == 429 and PLAN_UPGRADE_ERROR.lower() in err_body.lower():
                logging.error(
                    "OpenAlex says this request needs a paid plan (HTTP 429 '%s').",
                    PLAN_UPGRADE_ERROR,
                )
                break
            if e.code in {429, 500, 502, 503, 504} and attempt < max_retries:
                delay = min(1.5 * (2**attempt), 15.0) + random.uniform(0, 0.5)
                logging.info(
                    "OpenAlex request returned HTTP %s; retrying in %.1fs (%d/%d)",
                    e.code,
                    delay,
                    attempt + 1,
                    max_retries + 1,
                )
                time.sleep(delay)
                continue
            logging.error("HTTP Error %s while fetching %s: %s", e.code, url, err_body or e)
            break
        except OSError as e:
            if attempt < max_retries:
                time.sleep(1.5 * (2**attempt))
                continue
            logging.error("Network error while fetching %s: %s", url, e)
            break

    if exit_on_error:
        sys.exit(1)
    return None


def print_json(data: Any) -> None:
    output = json.dumps(data, indent=2)
    if not sys.stdout.isatty():
        print(output)
        return
    lines = output.splitlines()
    if len(lines) > TRUNCATE_LINE_LIMIT:
        remaining = len(lines) - TRUNCATE_LINE_LIMIT
        print("\n".join(lines[:TRUNCATE_LINE_LIMIT]))
        logging.warning(
            "Output truncated. %d additional lines not shown. Redirect output to a file if needed.",
            remaining,
        )
    else:
        print(output)


def handle_resolve(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/{args.entity_type}"
    params = {
        "search": args.query,
        "per_page": max(1, min(args.per_page, MAX_PER_PAGE)),
    }
    data = fetch_with_retry(url, params, api_key=REDACTED
    if data is None:
        sys.exit(1)
    results = [
        {
            "id": item.get("id"),
            "display_name": item.get("display_name"),
            "hint": item.get("hint") or item.get("works_count"),
        }
        for item in data.get("results", [])
    ]
    print_json(results)


_OPENALEX_SHORT_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z]\d+$")


def _is_valid_entity_id(entity_id: str) -> bool:
    return bool(
        _OPENALEX_SHORT_ID_RE.match(entity_id)
        or entity_id.startswith("https://openalex.org/")
        or entity_id.startswith("https://doi.org/")
    )


def handle_get(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    if not _is_valid_entity_id(args.id):
        logging.error(
            "Invalid entity ID %r. Expected a short ID (e.g. W2741809807), "
            "a full OpenAlex URL, or a DOI URL.",
            args.id,
        )
        sys.exit(1)
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/{args.entity_type}/{args.id}"
    params: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if args.select is not None:
        params["select"] = args.select
    data = fetch_with_retry(url, params, api_key=REDACTED
    print_json(data)


def _is_valid_pdf(data: bytes) -> bool:
    return data[:5] == b"%PDF-"


def _try_download_url(url: str, output_path: str) -> bool:
    try:
        data, _ = _http_get(url, timeout=PDF_TIMEOUT_SECS)
        if not _is_valid_pdf(data):
            return False
        out_dir = os.path.dirname(output_path)
        if out_dir:
            os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
        with open(output_path, "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
        return True
    except Exception as e:
        logging.warning("Failed to download from %s: %s", url, e)
        return False


def handle_download_pdf(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    url = _build_url_with_api_key(f"{PDF_BASE_URL}/works/{args.id}.pdf", args.api_key)
    if _try_download_url(url, args.output):
        logging.info("Successfully downloaded PDF to %s", args.output)
        return

    work_url = f"{BASE_URL}/works/{args.id}"
    work_data = fetch_with_retry(work_url, {}, api_key=REDACTED, exit_on_error=False)
    if work_data:
        locations = work_data.get("locations", [])
        if not locations and "best_oa_location" in work_data:
            locations = [work_data["best_oa_location"]]
        for loc in locations:
            if loc and loc.get("pdf_url") and _try_download_url(loc["pdf_url"], args.output):
                logging.info("Successfully downloaded PDF from fallback location.")
                return
    logging.error("Could not download PDF for %s.", args.id)
    sys.exit(1)


def handle_filter(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/{args.entity_type}"
    optional_params = ["search", "filter", "group_by", "sample", "seed", "select"]
    params = {
        k: getattr(args, k)
        for k in optional_params
        if getattr(args, k) is not None
    }
    if args.sort is not None and args.sample is None:
        params["sort"] = args.sort
    if args.group_by is None and args.sample is None:
        params["per_page"] = max(1, min(args.per_page, MAX_PER_PAGE))
        params["page"] = args.page
    data = fetch_with_retry(url, params, api_key=REDACTED
    print_json(data)


def handle_rate_limit(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/works"
    data = fetch_with_retry(url, {"per_page": 1}, api_key=REDACTED, return_headers=True)
    if data is None:
        sys.exit(1)
    headers = data.pop("_response_headers", {})
    limits = {
        "authenticated": bool(args.api_key),
        "x-ratelimit-limit": headers.get("x-ratelimit-limit"),
        "x-ratelimit-remaining": headers.get("x-ratelimit-remaining"),
        "x-ratelimit-reset": headers.get("x-ratelimit-reset"),
    }
    print_json({"rate_limits": limits})


def main(argv: Sequence[str]) -> None:
    _load_dotenv_if_present()
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="OpenAlex API CLI Utility")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--api-key",
        type=str,
        default=os.environ.get("OPENALEX_API_KEY"),
        help="Optional API key for higher rate limits.",
    )
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    parser_resolve = subparsers.add_parser("resolve", help="Resolve an entity name to its OpenAlex ID")
    parser_resolve.add_argument("entity_type", choices=ENTITY_TYPES)
    parser_resolve.add_argument("query", help="Name or part of the name to search for")
    parser_resolve.add_argument("--per-page", type=int, default=RESOLVE_PER_PAGE)
    parser_resolve.set_defaults(func=handle_resolve)

    parser_get = subparsers.add_parser("get", help="Get a single entity by its ID")
    parser_get.add_argument("entity_type", choices=ENTITY_TYPES)
    parser_get.add_argument("id", help="The OpenAlex ID (e.g., W2741809807)")
    parser_get.add_argument("--select", type=str, help="Limit returned fields")
    parser_get.set_defaults(func=handle_get)

    parser_pdf = subparsers.add_parser("download-pdf", help="Download PDF for a work")
    parser_pdf.add_argument("id", help="The OpenAlex Work ID")
    parser_pdf.add_argument("output", help="Output file path")
    parser_pdf.set_defaults(func=handle_download_pdf)

    parser_filter = subparsers.add_parser("filter", help="Filter and search entities")
    parser_filter.add_argument("entity_type", choices=ENTITY_TYPES)
    parser_filter.add_argument("--search", type=str)
    parser_filter.add_argument("--filter", type=str)
    parser_filter.add_argument("--sort", type=str)
    parser_filter.add_argument("--group-by", type=str)
    parser_filter.add_argument("--per-page", type=int, default=DEFAULT_PER_PAGE)
    parser_filter.add_argument("--page", type=int, default=1)
    parser_filter.add_argument("--sample", type=int)
    parser_filter.add_argument("--seed", type=int)
    parser_filter.add_argument("--select", type=str)
    parser_filter.set_defaults(func=handle_filter)

    parser_rate_limit = subparsers.add_parser("rate-limit", help="Check current rate limit status")
    parser_rate_limit.set_defaults(func=handle_rate_limit)

    args = parser.parse_args(argv[1:])
    args.func(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv)

## Summary – Release Highlights¶

Python 3.13 is a stable release of the Python programming language, with a mix of changes to the language, the implementation and the standard library. The biggest changes include a new interactive interpreter, experimental support for running in a free-threaded mode (PEP 703), and a Just-In-Time compiler (PEP 744).

The library changes contain removal of deprecated APIs and modules, as well as the usual improvements in user-friendliness and correctness. Several legacy standard library modules have now been removed following their deprecation in Python 3.11 (PEP 594).

This article doesn’t attempt to provide a complete specification of all new features, but instead gives a convenient overview. For full details refer to the documentation, such as the Library Reference and Language Reference. To understand the complete implementation and design rationale for a change, refer to the PEP for a particular new feature; but note that PEPs usually are not kept up-to-date once a feature has been fully implemented. See Porting to Python 3.13 for guidance on upgrading from earlier versions of Python.

Interpreter improvements:

- A greatly improved interactive interpreter and improved error messages.
- PEP 667: The `locals()` builtin now has defined semantics when mutating the returned mapping. Python debuggers and similar tools may now more reliably update local variables in optimized scopes even during concurrent code execution.
- PEP 703: CPython 3.13 has experimental support for running with the global interpreter lock disabled. See Free-threaded CPython for more details.
- PEP 744: A basic JIT compiler was added. It is currently disabled by default (though we may turn it on later). Performance improvements are modest – we expect to improve this over the next few releases.
- Color support in the new interactive interpreter, as well as in tracebacks and doctest output. This can be disabled through the `PYTHON_COLORS` and `NO_COLOR` environment variables.

Python data model improvements:

- `__static_attributes__` stores the names of attributes accessed through `self.X` in any function in a class body.
- `__firstlineno__` records the first line number of a class definition.

Significant improvements in the standard library:

- Add a new `PythonFinalizationError` exception, raised when an operation is blocked during finalization.
- The `argparse` module now supports deprecating command-line options, positional arguments, and subcommands.

- The `copy` module now has a `copy.replace()` function, with support for many builtin types and any class defining the `__replace__()` method.
- The new `dbm.sqlite3` module is now the default `dbm` backend.
- The `os` module has a suite of new functions for working with Linux’s timer notification file descriptors.
- The `random` module now has a command-line interface.

Security improvements:

- `ssl.create_default_context()` sets `ssl.VERIFY_X509_PARTIAL_CHAIN` and `ssl.VERIFY_X509_STRICT` as default flags.

C API improvements:

- The `Py_mod_gil` slot is now used to indicate that an extension module supports running with the GIL disabled.
- The PyTime C API has been added, providing access to system clocks.
- `PyMutex` is a new lightweight mutex that occupies a single byte.
- There is a new suite of functions for generating PEP 669 monitoring events in the C API.

"""Web search and fetch tools connected to the Exa MCP server.

Exa provides neural semantic web search, webpage content extraction, and crawling
over MCP. The free endpoint operates at ``https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp`` without requiring
an API key, and accepts an optional ``EXA_API_KEY`` for higher rate limits.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
from typing import Any
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from src.config.settings import get_settings
from src.modules.runs.tools import Tool, ToolContext, ToolResult

EXA_USER_AGENT = "VigilAgent-ExaSearch/1.0 (https://exa.ai)"


class WebSearchExaArgs(BaseModel):
    """Arguments for the ``web_search_exa`` tool."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    query: str = Field(
        ...,
        min_length=1,
        description=(
            "Natural language search query. A semantically rich description of the ideal page, "
            "not just raw keywords. Optionally include category:<type> (e.g. category:company or category:people)."
        ),
    )
    objective: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Goal for this search turn; describe which documents should rank first, "
            "which should be excluded, and what specific facts or figures to extract."
        ),
    )
    numResults: int | None = Field(
        default=8,
        description="Number of search results to return (default: 8, max: 20).",
    )


class WebFetchExaArgs(BaseModel):
    """Arguments for the ``web_fetch_exa`` tool."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    urls: list[str] = Field(
        ...,
        min_length=1,
        description="URLs of webpages to read and extract as clean markdown.",
    )
    maxCharacters: int | None = Field(
        default=3000,
        description="Maximum characters to extract per page (default: 3000).",
    )


def _call_exa_mcp_sync(
    tool_name: str,
    arguments: dict[str, Any],
    exa_url: str,
    api_key: str | None = None,
    timeout: float = 30.0,
) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    """Execute one tool call against the Exa MCP server via HTTP StreamMCP."""
    payload = {
        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
        "id": 1,
        "method": "tools/call",
        "params": {
            "name": tool_name,
            "arguments": arguments,
        },
    }
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream",
        "User-Agent": EXA_USER_AGENT,
    }
    if api_key:
        headers["x-api-key"] = api_key

    req = urllib.request.Request(
        exa_url,
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
        headers=headers,
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
            body = resp.read().decode("utf-8")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        err_msg = ""
        try:
            err_msg = exc.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        except Exception:
            pass
        return f"Exa MCP HTTP {exc.code} error: {err_msg or exc.reason}", True
    except Exception as exc:
        return f"Exa MCP connection error: {exc}", True

    # Parse JSON or SSE data line
    data: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    for line in body.splitlines():
        trimmed = line.strip()
        if trimmed.startswith("data:"):
            try:
                data = json.loads(trimmed[len("data:"):].strip())
                break
            except ValueError:
                continue
    if data is None:
        try:
            data = json.loads(body)
        except ValueError:
            return body[:1000], False

    if "error" in data:
        return f"Exa MCP returned error: {data['error']}", True

    result = data.get("result", {})
    is_error = bool(result.get("isError", False))
    content = result.get("content", [])
    if isinstance(content, list):
        parts = [
            item.get("text", str(item)) if isinstance(item, dict) else str(item)
            for item in content
        ]
        return "\n\n".join(parts), is_error
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content, is_error
    return json.dumps(result, indent=2), is_error


async def web_search_exa(args: WebSearchExaArgs, context: ToolContext) -> ToolResult:
    """Execute live neural web search via the free Exa MCP server."""
    settings = get_settings()
    arguments: dict[str, Any] = {"query": args.query}
    if args.objective:
        arguments["objective"] = args.objective
    else:
        arguments["objective"] = f"Find relevant, up-to-date information for: {args.query}"
    if args.numResults:
        arguments["numResults"] = min(max(args.numResults, 1), 20)

    output, is_error = await asyncio.to_thread(
        _call_exa_mcp_sync,
        "web_search_exa",
        arguments,
        settings.EXA_MCP_URL,
        settings.EXA_API_KEY or None,
    )
    if is_error:
        return ToolResult.failure(output)
    return ToolResult.success(output)


async def web_fetch_exa(args: WebFetchExaArgs, context: ToolContext) -> ToolResult:
    """Extract full markdown webpage content for URLs via the Exa MCP server."""
    settings = get_settings()
    arguments: dict[str, Any] = {"urls": args.urls}
    if args.maxCharacters:
        arguments["maxCharacters"] = args.maxCharacters

    output, is_error = await asyncio.to_thread(
        _call_exa_mcp_sync,
        "web_fetch_exa",
        arguments,
        settings.EXA_MCP_URL,
        settings.EXA_API_KEY or None,
    )
    if is_error:
        return ToolResult.failure(output)
    return ToolResult.success(output)


EXA_TOOLS: tuple[Tool, ...] = (
    Tool.define(
        name="web_search_exa",
        description=(
            "Search the live web for any topic using Exa neural search. "
            "Returns clean, parsed markdown highlights from top search results. "
            "Best for finding current facts, news, documentation, companies, and people."
        ),
        level="local",
        args_model=WebSearchExaArgs,
        handler=web_search_exa,
    ),
    Tool.define(
        name="web_fetch_exa",
        description=(
            "Extract full webpage content as clean markdown from one or more known URLs using Exa. "
            "Use to inspect full documentation pages or articles found via web_search_exa."
        ),
        level="local",
        args_model=WebFetchExaArgs,
        handler=web_fetch_exa,
    ),
)


__all__ = [
    "EXA_TOOLS",
    "WebFetchExaArgs",
    "WebSearchExaArgs",
    "web_fetch_exa",
    "web_search_exa",
]

## Technical Communication & Writing Standards (ASD-STE100 & Emoji Guidelines)

Follow the core principles of ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English) and strict emoji restraint in all plans, explanations, comments, and documentation:

### 1. Emoji Restraint
- Avoid emojis in all text, plans, code comments, and documentation.
- Use emojis only when strictly necessary for technical context (such as terminal status markers or user-requested UI elements).
- In UI code and frontends, use vector icons (such as `lucide-react`) instead of emojis.

### 2. Core ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English) Principles
Apply these rules to produce clear, direct, and unambiguous technical writing:

1. **Sentence Length**:
   - Limit procedural sentences (instructions, actions, commands) to a maximum of 20 words.
   - Limit descriptive sentences (explanations, specifications) to a maximum of 25 words.
2. **One Thought per Sentence**:
   - Express only one thought, fact, or instruction in each sentence.
   - Do not combine multiple separate actions into a single sentence.
3. **Paragraph Structure**:
   - Limit paragraphs to a maximum of 6 sentences.
   - Restrict each paragraph to a single topic.
4. **Active Voice and Imperative Mood**:
   - Write instructions in the imperative mood ("Run the test script", "Create the configuration file").
   - Prefer active voice over passive voice ("The service processes the event" instead of "The event is processed by the service").
5. **Directness and Precision**:
   - State conditions before the action ("If the test fails, inspect the stack trace").
   - Avoid vague words, ambiguous quantifiers, and filler (do not use "some", "several", "etc.", "as needed", "approximately" when exact values or steps exist).
   - Provide concrete file paths, names, numbers, and exact commands.
6. **Controlled Vocabulary and Consistency**:
   - One word, one meaning: maintain uniform terms for technical components throughout the project.
   - Do not use different synonyms for the same concept or file.
7. **Verbs and Tenses**:
   - Use simple tenses: simple present, simple past, and simple future (`will`).
   - Avoid continuous or progressive forms (`-ing`) when a simple tense works.
   - Avoid complex auxiliary or subjunctive constructions ("would have been", "could possibly be").
8. **Noun Clusters**:
   - Do not string more than three nouns together.
   - Break up dense noun groups with prepositions (for example, "configuration file for the server" instead of "server configuration settings file").
9. **Procedural Layout**:
   - Present sequential steps in vertical numbered lists.
   - Present items of equal status in vertical bulleted lists.

### Root Causes Identified

1. **Multi-Turn Context Loss ("The session keeps clearing")**:
   - Each chat message creates a new `run_id`.
   - Previously, `RunLoop` loaded only the messages matching the current `run_id` (`SELECT * FROM messages WHERE run_id = :run_id`), ignoring all prior conversation turns in the same `session_id`.
   - When you sent follow-up messages such as `"Try again it should work"` or `"search the web"`, the agent had no memory of the previous turn.

2. **Auth Session Clearing Race Condition**:
   - `SqlAuthStore.create_device` and `SqlChatRepository.create_session` called `session.flush()` without `session.commit()`.
   - FastAPI sent the HTTP response before the post-yield `session.commit()` completed.
   - Immediate follow-up requests (`GET /auth/me`) read uncommitted state on another pool connection, returned `401 Unauthorized`, and triggered `expire()`, wiping the IndexedDB session.

3. **Missing `vigil-sandbox:latest` Image & Host-Only Tool Execution**:
   - `RunToolExecutor.execute` attempted to start a `vigil-sandbox:latest` Docker container before running any tool, including host-side tools like `web_search`.
   - Because `vigil-sandbox:latest` was not tagged locally and `/var/vigil/workspaces` was not writable by a non-root user, every tool call failed with `SandboxExecFailed`.

---

### Fixes Applied

1. **Multi-Turn Session Memory**:
   - Added `list_session_history` to [state.py](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/state.py) and wired it into `RunLoop._assemble` in [loop.py](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/loop.py).
   - Each new run in a chat session now loads prior user and assistant turns from the same `session_id`.

2. **Immediate Database Commits & Resilient Token Hydration**:
   - Added explicit `await self.session.commit()` calls to `SqlAuthStore` in [state.py](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/auth/state.py) and `SqlChatRepository` in [state.py](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/chat/state.py).
   - Updated [useSession.ts](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/store/useSession.ts) so transient errors or pairing races do not wipe the stored token.
   - Filtered intermediate tool-call thoughts out of `SqlChatRepository.get_history` so only user messages and final assistant replies appear in the chat history.

3. **Sandbox & Web Search Execution**:
   - Tagged `vigil-sandbox:latest` in Docker and added a writable `/tmp/vigil/workspaces` fallback in [sandbox.py](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/integrations/sandbox/sandbox.py) and [dependencies.py](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/dependencies.py).
   - Configured `RunToolExecutor.execute` in [dependencies.py](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/dependencies.py) to run `web_search`, `web_fetch`, and `manage_tasks` directly on the host without starting a container.
   - Embedded the background worker inside FastAPI's lifespan in [main.py](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/main.py) so `uvicorn --reload` automatically runs and reloads the worker.
